name: jdx
description: IDE for AI agents on JVM bytecode: members, method bodies, usages and call graphs. Requires a Java 21+ runtime on PATH or JAVA_HOME.
long_description:
jdx is an IDE for AI agents working on JVM code. Each tool answers one question: the members of a type, a single method body, usages, or a call graph, for jars, source directories, and the JDK.

Compatibility: Linux, macOS, and Windows. A Java 21 or newer runtime must be installed and available on PATH or via JAVA_HOME before the bundle is launched. The bundle contains the jdx launchers and the fat jar. Install a JDK or JRE separately.

The host launches bin/jdx with argument mcp over stdio. On Windows the platform override launches bin/jdx.bat with argument mcp. Tool names and descriptions are copied from `jdx mcp` tools/list.

tools.name: jdx_show
tools.description: Returns the class card for one type: kind, modifiers, supertypes, member counts, provenance, and the next command to run. Use it to see what a type is. Use jdx_members to list what you can call (inherited members included) and jdx_outline for members declared on this type only. A member reference is error code 3; use jdx_signature, jdx_doc, or jdx_body for a member. An ambiguous short name is not guessed: the call is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Structure comes from bytecode parsed with ASM. Never loads or executes the inspected class.

tools.name: jdx_members
tools.description: Returns the members you can call on a type. Inherited members are included by default and grouped by the declaring type; java.lang.Object collapses to one line unless from names it. This is the completion list. Use it for the callable surface. Use jdx_outline for one dense line per member declared on this type only, jdx_signature for one member's parameters, and jdx_show for the type card. declared true limits the list to members declared on this exact type. An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Kotlin types render from @Metadata unless view is jvm. Parses with ASM and never loads or executes the inspected class.

tools.name: jdx_outline
tools.description: Returns one dense line per member declared on this exact type. Inherited members are never included. This is the file-structure view. Use it to scan what the type itself declares. Use jdx_members when you also need inherited members, and jdx_signature or jdx_body to open one member. An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Parses with ASM and never loads or executes the inspected class.

tools.name: jdx_body
tools.description: Returns one member's source body, sliced to that member, plus a provenance line naming the artifact and file. context adds lines around the slice; maxLines caps it (default 200). Use it to read an implementation. Use jdx_signature for the declaration only, jdx_doc for javadoc, and jdx_source for the whole file or an arbitrary line window. Paired sources are sliced verbatim. Without them, or when engine is set, the body is decompiled and the provenance line is marked ⚠ reconstructed. An ambiguous ref is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Overload choice is decided from bytecode before sources or a decompiler run. Parses with ASM and never loads or executes the inspected class.

tools.name: jdx_source
tools.description: Returns a type's source file, or a slice of it, plus provenance. lines is a 1-based inclusive window A:B. around centers the slice on a member; context widens that window. maxLines caps the slice (default 200). Use it when one member is not enough. Use jdx_body for a single member body, jdx_outline for the member list, and jdx_doc for javadoc only. Paired sources are served verbatim. Without them, or when engine is set, the file is decompiled and the provenance line is marked ⚠ reconstructed. lines and around together are error code 3. An ambiguous type is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Parses with ASM and never loads or executes the inspected class.

tools.name: jdx_signature
tools.description: Returns one signature line per overload, with real parameter names, generics, throws and defaults, plus provenance. A name without a parameter list lists every overload. Use it for parameter info. Use jdx_body to read the code, jdx_doc for javadoc, and jdx_members to see every member of the type. A type reference with no member is error code 3. An ambiguous owner is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Kotlin signatures come from @Metadata unless view is jvm. Parses with ASM and never loads or executes the inspected class.

tools.name: jdx_doc
tools.description: Returns rendered javadoc for a type or member (HTML stripped, inline tags unwrapped) plus provenance. An undocumented member falls back to the nearest documenting supertype, and the answer says which one, unless no-inherited is true. Use it for the documentation. Use jdx_signature for the declaration, jdx_body for the code, and jdx_source for the file. The fallback stays on unless no-inherited is true; inherited is accepted for explicitness and inherited false leaves the fallback on. Setting both is error code 3. raw returns the verbatim comment. maxLines caps the text (default 200). An ambiguous member ref is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Never loads or executes the inspected class.

tools.name: jdx_search
tools.description: Returns symbols whose names match the query. Each hit carries its canonical ref, kind and artifact. Globs by default. regex true uses a Java regex. fuzzy true retries a miss by Levenshtein distance. A bare word matches case-insensitively or as camel humps (HMap finds HashMap). Use it to find a name anywhere on the classpath. Use jdx_resolve to expand one short name into candidates, jdx_ls for packages, and jdx_usages or jdx_callers once you have a ref. Default kind all covers types, packages and modules only. It does not scan methods or fields; a miss under that default points at kind method. Pass kind method or field to scan members. Nothing matched is error code 1. Member scans parse bytecode with ASM and never load or execute classes.

tools.name: jdx_resolve
tools.description: Returns every candidate for a short or partial name (a type, a member, or a package). Each row has a kind, an artifact, and a copy-pasteable canonical ref. Use it when a stack trace or snippet says Gson and you need the fully qualified ref. Use jdx_search for globs and regexes. Use jdx_show or jdx_members once one candidate is the one you want. Several candidates are a successful result (code 0). No candidate is error code 1, with did-you-mean suggestions. Parses with ASM and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_ls
tools.description: Returns packages in the workspace roots. A glob lists matching packages with type counts. An exact package name lists the types in that package. Use it to browse a library by package. Use jdx_tree for one artifact's package tree, and jdx_search to find a symbol by name. Omit query to list every package. Reads class names from bytecode and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_tree
tools.description: Returns artifacts and their package trees. query is an artifact-label glob. Omit it to cover every artifact. Use it to see how a jar is laid out. Use jdx_ls to list packages or the types in one exact package, and jdx_search to find a symbol. depth 0 shows only the top package segments (default depth is 8). counts adds a class count on each node. Reads class names from bytecode and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_usages
tools.description: Returns where a type or member is referenced across the workspace jars and source directories: one row per referencing method, or per mentioning line in a source directory. Bytecode rows carry file:line when the class has a LineNumberTable. Use it for find-usages across every edge kind. Use jdx_callers for the incoming call tree only, jdx_calls for what a method calls, jdx_samples for a few ranked snippets, and jdx_annotated to start from an annotation or a recipe alias. kind throw is methods that declare the type in throws, not ATHROW sites. kind impl and kind override are rejected (error code 3); use jdx_hierarchy and jdx_implementors. Source-directory hits are textual whole-word mentions and show up only as ref. where requires kind annotation. An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Scans bytecode roots on each call (no persistent index) and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_annotated
tools.description: Returns classes and members that carry an annotation. Each row includes the rendered use, for example @java.lang.Deprecated(forRemoval=true). Use it as the annotation-driven view. The listing matches jdx_usages with kind annotation, and query also accepts recipe aliases: deprecated (java.lang.Deprecated), forRemoval (@Deprecated(forRemoval=true)), test and junit5 (org.junit.jupiter.api.Test), junit4 (org.junit.Test), bean (org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean). A type or an annotation-use '@com.example.Tag(k=v)' (leading @ accepted) works too. Use jdx_usages for calls, reads, writes and the other edge kinds. An ambiguous type is error code 2 and lists every candidate. where clauses are AND-ed. Scans bytecode on each call and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_hierarchy
tools.description: Returns the type hierarchy: supertypes upward, interfaces included, and subtypes downward across the workspace. When both up and down are omitted or false, both directions are walked. Set one of them true and the other false to walk only that way. Use it for the full picture. Use jdx_implementors for subtypes and implementors only. A member reference is error code 3. direct limits the walk to one level. in and exclude filter subtypes by artifact label. Omit depth for an unlimited walk (must be >= 1 when set). An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Scans bytecode roots on each call and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_implementors
tools.description: Returns who implements this interface or extends this class, transitively. This is the downward half of the hierarchy. Use it for "who implements this?". Use jdx_hierarchy when you also need supertypes. direct keeps only immediate children. A member reference is error code 3. Omit depth for an unlimited walk. An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Scans bytecode roots on each call and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_callers
tools.description: Returns who calls this method, as a depth-bounded tree (default depth 1, direct callers). Override-aware: call sites through overrides and declaring supertypes are included. Constructors, static methods and private methods stay exact. exact true matches invoke owners only. A cycle is marked …(cycle). Use it for the incoming call hierarchy. Use jdx_usages for every reference kind (reads, writes, annotations, throws declarations) as a flat list, jdx_calls for what this method calls, and jdx_samples for ranked example snippets. Type and field references are error code 3. An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Scans bytecode roots on each call and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_calls
tools.description: Returns what this method calls, as a depth-bounded tree (default depth 1, direct callees). Callees are bytecode-exact: the invoke instruction names one owner. Override expansion is only on jdx_callers. A cycle is marked …(cycle). Use it for the outgoing call hierarchy. Use jdx_callers for incoming callers, jdx_usages for a flat list of every reference kind, and jdx_samples for example snippets. externalOnly drops callees in the method's own artifact. Type and field references are error code 3. An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Scans bytecode roots on each call and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_samples
tools.description: Returns a few real call sites for a symbol, ranked non-test before test, non-generated before generated, and fuller overloads first. Each row is the calling method. Paired sources supply an enclosing-method snippet; without them the row is location-only. The default limit is 3. maxLines caps each snippet (default 15). Use it to see how a symbol is actually called. Use jdx_usages for the full reference list, jdx_callers for the incoming call tree, and jdx_body to open one caller. A type ref matches calls to any of its members. A field ref is error code 3. An ambiguous short name is error code 2 and lists every candidate. Scans bytecode roots on each call and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_literals
tools.description: Returns string constants that contain query: bytecode LDC loads, String field ConstantValue entries, and .properties resource keys and values. A properties hit is reported as prop path#key with the property value. Use it to find a literal such as a message key or a URL fragment. Use jdx_search to find symbols by name, and jdx_resources to list resource paths rather than property text. Substring match by default. regex true treats query as a Java regex. ignoreCase applies to substring mode only. Nothing matched is error code 1. Scans bytecode and resource entries on each call and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_services
tools.description: Returns META-INF/services SPI registrations across the workspace jars: the service interface and each provider class. Use it to see who provides a service interface. JPMS module-info provides and uses are jdx_modules; this tool reads only META-INF/services. Omit query to list every registration. A query matches the service interface name or a provider class name. Nothing matched is error code 1. Reads the service files as text and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_modules
tools.description: Returns JPMS module-info descriptors: requires, exports, opens, uses and provides. Use it for module metadata. META-INF/services registrations are jdx_services. MANIFEST.MF attributes are jdx_manifest. This tool reads module-info only. Omit query to list every module. A query matches the module name, an exported or opened package, a uses or provides service, or a provider class. Nothing matched is error code 1. Parses module-info with ASM and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_manifest
tools.description: Returns META-INF/MANIFEST.MF attributes. The default section is the main attributes (Main-Class, Implementation-Version, Multi-Release, and the rest). entries true switches to per-entry JarEntry attributes (Name sections such as digests and Content-Type). Use it for manifest metadata. Resource paths and file text are jdx_resources. module-info is jdx_modules. This tool does not extract resource bytes. Omit query to list every attribute in the selected section. A query matches the attribute name or value, and the entry path when entries is true. Nothing matched is error code 1. Reads manifest text and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_resources
tools.description: Returns non-class resource paths across the workspace jars, including META-INF, .properties and versioned META-INF/versions copies, stored as the path is written. Omit query to list every path. A query matches the entry path. Use it to find a resource file. Manifest attributes are jdx_manifest. SPI registrations are jdx_services. String constants and property text are jdx_literals. cat true prints the unique match's text instead of listing paths, and then query is required. More than one match with cat is error code 2 and lists each path with its artifact. Binary or non-UTF-8 payloads are not dumped; the answer reports the size. maxLines caps cat text (default 200). limit applies to listing. Nothing matched is error code 1. Reads zip entries and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_diff
tools.description: Returns a public-API diff between two artifacts, using named binary-compatibility rules such as MEMBER_REMOVED and RETURN_TYPE_CHANGED, most breaking first. query is the old artifact and new is the candidate. Each side is a jar path, a class directory, a glob, or a Maven coordinate group:artifact:version. No other jdx_* tool compares two artifacts. The comparison itself is code 0 whatever it found. failOn breaking or any turns a tripped gate into code 1, and result.gate carries the same verdict. visibility public (the default) keeps public and protected declarations; all includes every declared type and member. severity changes which findings are printed; the tally still describes the whole comparison. Maven coordinates resolve from the local Gradle and Maven caches only. This server has no fetch parameter and never downloads. A side that resolves to two artifacts is error code 3. Bytecode only: no sources and no decompiler. Parses with ASM and never loads or executes classes.

tools.name: jdx_version
tools.description: Returns the jdx version this server was built as, in result.version of the JSON envelope. Use it to check which build is answering. Use jdx_health for liveness (uptime, workspace, queries answered). jdx_doctor does not run over MCP; run `jdx doctor` in a shell. query is an optional label echoed back and may be empty. Does not read jars.

tools.name: jdx_doctor
tools.description: Refuses to run over MCP and returns error code 6. jdx doctor reports the machine it runs on, which would be this server's host rather than the client's. Run `jdx doctor` in a shell on the machine you want diagnosed. Use jdx_version for the build identity and jdx_health to see whether this server is answering. query is an optional label and is not consulted.

tools.name: jdx_health
tools.description: Returns a liveness snapshot for this process: workspace, uptimeSeconds, queryCount, indexedArtifacts (always 0), indexMode "live-roots-first", rpcVersion, appVersion, pid and memoryUsedMb. queryCount counts tool calls this process has answered, including this one. Use it to check that the server is up. indexedArtifacts stays 0 because usages, hierarchy and call queries re-scan bytecode roots per call; there is no persistent index yet. Use jdx_version for the build string alone. query is an optional label echoed back. Does not scan jars.
